title: The G7 Russian Oil Price Cap Assumed Western Insurance Was Indispensable. Russia Built a 1,100-Vessel Shadow Fleet With Fake P&I Certificates, Fraudulent Flags, and Naval Escorts. Only 118 Vessels Are Sanctioned. That's 10 Percent (2022 to 2026)
narrative: The G7 oil price cap on Russian crude, set at $60 per barrel, was designed to limit Russia's war revenue while keeping oil flowing to global markets. Western maritime insurers were prohibited from covering tankers carrying Russian oil sold above the cap. In response, Russia assembled a "shadow fleet" of aging tankers with opaque ownership, questionable insurance, and flags of convenience. By 2026, this fleet had grown to over 1,100 vessels, moving the majority of Russian seaborne oil exports outside Western regulatory reach.
telemetry: Shadow fleet: 600 ships (end 2022) → 1,100-1,400 (Dec 2023) → "more than tripled" by 2025
Only 118 vessels sanctioned across US, EU, and UK combined, out of 1,100+
Russian crude: 1,400M barrels exported by ship in 2022; ~3.64M b/d seaborne by May 2023
China and India buy ~87% of Russian seaborne crude exports
Price cap: $60/bbl set Dec 2022; Russian crude dipped to $49 (Jan 2023) → exceeded cap at $73 (Aug 2023)
By Aug 2023, 50%+ of Russian oil moved by shadow fleet outside Western insurance
Ro Marine (Oslo) fake P&I certificate scandal exposed by Danwatch/NRK — vessels presented falsified insurance documents
Two-thirds of shadow fleet has "unknown" insurers per Windward AI
Flag state explosion: Gabon registry went from ~0 to 98% high-risk vessels; Cook Islands, Comoros, Djibouti, Guinea, Benin all new shadow fleet flags
367 false-flagged tankers identified by April 2026; 21 inter-linked fraudulent registry networks
Russian Navy escorting tankers since June 2025 through high-risk zones
Black Sea oil spill Dec 2024 from shadow fleet tanker Volgoneft-212 — 4,300 tons of fuel oil into Kerch Strait
analysis:
The G7 price cap was designed as a precision economic weapon. It has become a precision failure. The cap architecture assumes Western control of maritime insurance — a valid assumption in 2022, when the International Group of P&I Clubs covered 90% of global tanker tonnage. But the shadow fleet bypasses insurance entirely. Ro Marine in Oslo was exposed issuing fake P&I certificates to shadow fleet vessels — certificates that looked legitimate to port authorities but had no backing. Two-thirds of shadow fleet vessels now have "unknown" insurers. The insurance lever has snapped.

The flag state data reveals deliberate regulatory arbitrage. Gabon's registry exploded from near-zero to serving as a flag for 98% high-risk vessels — this is not organic maritime growth, it is a business model. Cook Islands, Comoros, Djibouti, Guinea, and Benin have followed the same playbook. Twenty-one inter-linked fraudulent registry networks were identified by April 2026. The flag state system assumes states have an interest in enforcing standards; these states have an interest in avoiding them.

The sanction numbers are the most damning. Only 118 vessels sanctioned out of 1,100+ in the shadow fleet. That is roughly 10%. The remaining 90% operate freely, loading at Russian ports, transiting the Turkish Straits, delivering to Indian and Chinese refineries, and returning for another load. The enforcement gap is not a bug — it is the design. Sanctioning all 1,100 vessels would spike oil prices and trigger a global recession. The G7 has chosen partial enforcement because full enforcement is economically impossible.

The Russian Navy escort mission, initiated in June 2025, adds a military dimension. Tankers are now escorted by warships through high-risk zones. This transforms commercial vessels into military-protected assets — a blurring of lines that makes any enforcement action against a shadow fleet tanker a potential military confrontation.
verdict: The G7 oil price cap failed because it was designed for a world where Western insurance was indispensable — but Russia built a 1,100-vessel shadow fleet with fake certificates, fraudulent flags, and naval escorts, and the G7 chose to sanction only 10% of it because full enforcement would crash the global economy.
